standard.title: Identity shaped by language, culture, attitudes and values
standard.description: reflect on and explain how their own and others' identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), attitudes, beliefs and values
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can recognise how language reflects cultural practices and identity, and have reflected on their own intercultural positioning (AC9LCH6U04). They have explored language variation across communities. They have not yet examined how attitudes, beliefs and values shape communication style, reflected on how cultural events and practices change across contexts, or critically examined stereotyping in intercultural interaction.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students reflect on and explain how their own and others' identity is shaped by language, culture, attitudes, beliefs and values — including how these factors influence communication style, cultural participation, and intercultural understanding.

nodes.label: Attitudes, beliefs and values shaping communication
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how attitudes, beliefs and values — in both their own and others' backgrounds — shape communication choices in the target language and English.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two ways that attitudes, beliefs or values shape communication style in the target language community, and compare with at least one way these factors shape communication in English-speaking contexts.
nodes.typical_width: Reflect on how attitudes, beliefs and values are reflected in language and gesture in everyday conversations and media; examine how cultural background shapes communication style; compare communication norms across cultural contexts; identify how First Nations Australian languages connect to Country and compare with target language cultural connections.
wider: Analyse a real or fictional intercultural interaction — identify every moment where attitudes, beliefs or values are visible in a language or gesture choice, and explain the cultural logic behind each
Compare how a specific belief or value (e.g. about respect, family, community) shapes language use differently in the target language community and in own family or community context
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding how attitudes and values shape communication is the conceptual prerequisite for all intercultural reflection at this level. Students who cannot see the value system behind communication choices cannot reflect meaningfully on their own identity or explain others' behaviour.

response_modes.reason: Values-to-communication analysis requires explicit scaffolding — students need a framework for moving from 'they communicate differently' to 'this is the belief or value that produces this communication pattern.' Guided analysis with cultural context information builds this explanatory capacity.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two ways attitudes, beliefs or values shape communication in the target language community
Compares these with at least one parallel example from English-speaking contexts

nodes.label: Cultural participation and identity across contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can reflect on how cultural practices and events shape identity, and discuss how participation in cultural events changes across different contexts and regions.
nodes.minimum_width: Reflect on at least one cultural event or practice in which they participate and explain how it shapes or expresses their identity, noting how the practice may vary across contexts or regions.
nodes.typical_width: Reflect on participation in cultural events and how practices change across contexts and regions; examine how family origins and multilingual background shape language use and identity; discuss how mixing languages reflects cultural identity; consider how cultural practices in diaspora communities differ from homeland practices.
wider: Research how a specific cultural practice has changed in the diaspora context compared with the homeland — explain the factors that caused the change and discuss what this reveals about how identity adapts across contexts

Reflect on own family's cultural practices — identify what has been maintained, what has changed, and what this reveals about the relationship between language, culture and identity across generations

response_modes.reason: Identity-through-cultural-participation is understood through varied reflective encounters — different events, different community contexts, different generational perspectives. Single-event reflection produces limited insight; varied cultural reflection builds the richer identity narrative the descriptor requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background learners navigate complex cultural identities across homeland, diaspora, school and community contexts. Width investment here — particularly in tasks that explore intergenerational and cross-context cultural change — activates this unique lived experience as a source of genuine insight.
success_criteria: Reflects on at least one cultural event or practice and explains how it shapes their identity
Notes at least one way the practice varies across contexts, regions, or generations

nodes.label: Stereotyping, sensitivity and intercultural self-awareness
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify stereotyping risks in intercultural interactions, demonstrate sensitivity in cross-cultural questioning, and reflect on their own communication adaptations when interacting across cultural contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one stereotyping risk in intercultural interaction and explain a strategy for avoiding it, and reflect on at least one specific communication adaptation they make when interacting across cultural contexts.
nodes.typical_width: Develop awareness of stereotyping in intercultural interactions; practise sensitive and considerate questioning; reflect on own communication style adaptations when interacting in different cultural contexts; discuss how some cultural behaviours may be misinterpreted across cultural contexts.
wider: Analyse a case of cultural misinterpretation — identify the stereotyping or assumption at work, explain the cultural logic of both sides, and propose how the misunderstanding could have been prevented
Reflect on a personal experience of cultural misunderstanding or misinterpretation — analyse what assumptions were made, what was misread, and what was learned from the experience

response_modes.reason: Stereotyping awareness and intercultural self-reflection integrate values analysis (node 1) and cultural identity reflection (node 2) into a mature intercultural stance. The teaching investment is in creating genuinely reflective conditions — real or realistic intercultural scenarios — where students examine their own assumptions rather than only others'.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one stereotyping risk in intercultural interaction and explains a strategy for avoiding it
Reflects on at least one specific communication adaptation they make when interacting across cultural contexts
